short: A British nuclear-powered submarine and the only one to have sunk an enemy ship with torpedoes.
full:
Commissioned on 9 November 1971, HMS Conqueror (S48) was a Churchill-class nuclear-powered fleet submarine of the Royal Navy. It was designed to hunt Soviet submarines during the Cold War but became famous for its role in the 1982 Falklands War. On 2 May 1982, under the command of Commander Chris Wreford-Brown, it fired three Mark 8 torpedoes at the Argentine cruiser ARA General Belgrano, striking it twice and sinking it with heavy loss of life.

The sinking of the Belgrano demonstrated the absolute dominance of nuclear submarines in modern naval warfare, effectively forcing the entire Argentine surface fleet back to port for the remainder of the conflict. Conqueror remains the only nuclear-powered submarine to have ever engaged and sunk an enemy surface ship with torpedoes. It was decommissioned on 2 August 1990 after nineteen years of service.
